decisionMemo.businessProblem: A B2B marketplace growing 30% is leaking its most valuable GMV: seller NRR fell from 108% to 95%, and the top 8% of sellers (61% of GMV) are routing repeat buyers off-platform after the first marketplace-sourced order (on-platform large-seller repeat rate fell 64%→41%, ~30% of their repeat GMV now off-platform). The owner reads this as declining seller satisfaction and value proposition and wants broad seller-success investment and new features. But the problem is concentrated and structural: a flat ~12% take-rate is cheap for demand-dependent small/mid sellers (whose retention and satisfaction are stable) and economically irrational for high-volume repeat sellers, who pay 12% on buyers the marketplace no longer sources, making disintermediation the rational move (their top complaint, 58%, is 'commission too high for repeat orders'). With the next raise gated on GMV/retention and 24 months of runway, the owner must decide whether to spread seller-success effort broadly or restructure monetization for the large-seller segment before more GMV leaks.
